match.reason: The bank point teaches the activity series and displacement reactions, while the new point asks for the general properties of metals and non-metals and where they sit on the periodic table, so no bank point teaches the same idea.

draft.title: Metals and non-metals
card: Metals are usually shiny. They conduct heat and electricity well, and they can be bent or hammered into shape without breaking.
Non-metals are usually dull. They are poor conductors of heat and electricity, called insulators, and solid ones are brittle, so they shatter when hit.
On the periodic table, metals sit to the left and in the middle. Non-metals sit to the right.
These are general patterns. A few elements break them, such as carbon in the form of graphite, which is a non-metal that conducts electricity.
draft.remember: Metals are shiny, bendable conductors on the left. Non-metals are dull, brittle insulators on the right.

a.q: A strip of an unknown element is shiny, bends without snapping and lets electricity flow through it. Where on the periodic table is it most likely to sit?
opts: On the left or in the middle
On the far right
In the top right corner only
It could be anywhere, as position tells nothing
a.why: Shiny, bendable and conducting are the properties of a metal, and metals sit to the left and in the middle. The far right holds non-metals, which are usually dull insulators.
a.clue: Shiny, bendable and conducting describe one type of element.

b.q: Sam hits a lump of an element with a hammer and it shatters into pieces. It is dull and does not light a small bulb in a circuit. What should Sam conclude?
opts: It is most likely a non-metal
It is most likely a metal
It is a metal that has gone dull with age
It is a metal, because all solids conduct electricity
b.why: Shattering, a dull surface and failing to conduct are all properties of a non-metal. Metals bend rather than shatter, and they conduct, so a metal would not fit all three results.
b.clue: Think about what a metal does when hit, and whether it would conduct.

a.best: On the left or in the middle

b.best: It is most likely a non-metal

problems.detail: The remember line places metals only 'on the left', but the card says 'to the left and in the middle', and question a's answer depends on the middle.
